title: Rank Employees Universally by Salary with Unique Row Numbers
description_markdown: Assign a unique sequence rank to every employee ordered by `salary` DESC, `emp_id` ASC using `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC, emp_id ASC)` as `sal_seq`. Return `emp_id`, `first_name`, `salary`, and `sal_seq`. Order by `sal_seq` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Universal row number ranking
SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC, emp_id ASC) AS sal_seq
FROM employees
ORDER BY sal_seq ASC;
solution_query: SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC, emp_id ASC) AS sal_seq FROM employees ORDER BY sal_seq ASC;
solution_explanation: ROW_NUMBER() generates a continuous, non-repeating integer sequence across the ordered partition.
common_mistakes: Omitting the secondary tie-breaker in ORDER BY causing non-deterministic row numbers.
interview_tip: Always include a unique primary key column in the ROW_NUMBER() ORDER BY clause for deterministic output.
hints: Use `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC, emp_id ASC) AS sal_seq`.
Order outer query by `sal_seq ASC`.
Query: SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC, emp_id ASC) AS sal_seq FROM employees ORDER BY sal_seq ASC;

title: Rank Courses by Enrollment Volume
description_markdown: In a CTE, compute total enrollments per course: `c.course_id`, `c.course_code`, and `COUNT(e.enrollment_id) AS total_enrolled` from `courses c` left joined to `enrollments e` on `c.course_id = e.course_id` grouped by `c.course_id`, `c.course_code`. In the main query, assign `DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_enrolled DESC)` as `enrollment_rank`. Return `course_code`, `total_enrolled`, and `enrollment_rank`. Order by `enrollment_rank` ASC, `course_code` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Rank courses by enrollment
WITH course_counts AS (
  SELECT c.course_id, c.course_code, COUNT(e.enrollment_id) AS total_enrolled
  FROM courses c
  LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id
  GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_code
)
SELECT course_code, total_enrolled,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_enrolled DESC) AS enrollment_rank
FROM course_counts
ORDER BY enrollment_rank ASC, course_code ASC;
solution_query: WITH course_counts AS (SELECT c.course_id, c.course_code, COUNT(e.enrollment_id) AS total_enrolled FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_code) SELECT course_code, total_enrolled, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_enrolled DESC) AS enrollment_rank FROM course_counts ORDER BY enrollment_rank ASC, course_code ASC;
solution_explanation: Combines aggregate group counts with window ranking in an outer query.
common_mistakes: Using INNER JOIN which discards courses with zero registrations.
interview_tip: LEFT JOIN preserves zero-count rows before passing to window ranking.
